## The vapour column repair {#sec-ch08-fixvapor}

### Summary

When the borrow of @sec-ch08-borrow cannot cover a deficit from the parent vapour in the same cell, the vapour itself
goes negative. A local repair has no mass to work with. The column repair is the fallback: it looks along the $x_1$
column for mass to move, the whole column on the two stage calls and the block's piece of it on the others.
It moves only the deficit. The negative cells go to zero, and the cells below that cover them each give up the same
fraction of their vapour, so a deficit of $10^{-11}$ moves a moist cell by $10^{-11}$ and no more. The redo mark
follows the deficit, not the donors: a deficit below round-off of the cell's gas density is repaired without a
redo.[^ch08-fixvapor-alias]

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Repair a negative vapour by borrowing its deficit from the cells below, in proportion to their vapour; @eq-ch08-fixvapor-borrow.

**Data.** In: the interior vapour and cloud rows, the dry density, the cell volumes. Out: the rows repaired in place, or an error.

**Placement.** Inside the conserved pass of @sec-ch08-eoslimiter, after the borrow.

**Activation.** With the limiter, where a vapour row is negative, or a parentless cloud after the borrow.

**Guarantee / limits.** Conserves the column mass it sees; donors move by the deficit only; vapour throws, clouds clamp.

**Evidence.** `test_fix_vapor_deficit.<b>` (run at the pin), `test_fix_vapor_volume.<b>`, the failure ctests; no report check.
:::

Local symbols: $\mathcal M$ is the window of $x_1$ cells one scan step rewrites; $D$ and $Q$ [kg m$^{-3}$, per
bottom-cell volume] are the window's deficit and the vapour of its donor cells. $\rho_{n,l}$ and $V_l$ are the partial
density and the volume of cell $l$, as in @sec-appa.

### Derivation

The repair is a redistribution, so the thing to establish is what it moves and what it conserves.
It weights by cell volume at
`cell_volume` ({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}), which is the
point recorded in the code comment there. A column repair that moved *densities* would not conserve mass on a
non-uniform grid, because equal densities in unequal cells are unequal masses. Weighting by volume makes the
redistribution conservative in mass.

**What one scan step moves.** Index the column from the bottom, $l = 0..N-1$. The kernel `fix_vapor_impl` scans from
the top ({{< code src/eos/fix_vapor_impl.h fix_vapor_impl >}}). A negative cell starts a window $\mathcal M$ that grows
downward until its volume-weighted vapour sum is non-negative. Split the window into its negative and non-negative
cells and sum each part:

$$
D = -\sum_{l\in\mathcal M,\ \rho_{n,l}<0} \frac{V_l}{V_0}\,\rho_{n,l} ,\qquad
Q = \sum_{l\in\mathcal M,\ \rho_{n,l}\ge0} \frac{V_l}{V_0}\,\rho_{n,l} .
$$ {#eq-ch08-fixvapor-sums}

$D$ is the deficit and $Q$ the vapour the donor cells hold; both are `deficit` and `donors`
({{< code src/eos/fix_vapor_impl.h fix_vapor_impl >}}). The window stops growing at the first cell that makes
$Q - D \ge 0$. Every cell of the window is then rewritten as

$$
\rho_{n,l} \leftarrow
\begin{cases}
0, & \rho_{n,l} < 0,\\[2pt]
\rho_{n,l} - \rho_{n,l}\,\dfrac{D}{Q}, & \rho_{n,l} \ge 0,
\end{cases}
\qquad l\in\mathcal M ,
$$ {#eq-ch08-fixvapor-borrow}

which is the loop over `share` ({{< code src/eos/fix_vapor_impl.h fix_vapor_impl >}}). Three properties follow, each in
one line.

1. *Mass is kept.* Multiply @eq-ch08-fixvapor-borrow by $V_l/V_0$ and sum over $\mathcal M$. The negative cells
   contribute $0$ after and $-D$ before. The donors contribute $Q - Q\,D/Q = Q - D$ after and $Q$ before. Both sums are
   $Q - D$.
2. *Nothing goes negative.* The window stopped where $Q - D \ge 0$, so $D/Q \le 1$ and each donor keeps
   $(1 - D/Q)\,\rho_{n,l} \ge 0$. The window holds at least one negative cell, so $D > 0$, and $Q - D \ge 0$ then
   needs $Q > 0$: the division is always defined here. The code guards it anyway, with a share of zero for $Q = 0$
   (`share`, {{< code src/eos/fix_vapor_impl.h fix_vapor_impl >}}).
3. *The donors move by the deficit only.* Donor $l$ loses $\rho_{n,l}D/Q$, and the donors together lose $D$,
   whatever their vapour. The dry density does not enter @eq-ch08-fixvapor-borrow. So a deficit at round-off size moves
   the cells below it at round-off size.

The branch that runs when the window passes the bottom with $Q - D < 0$ is a different one: it zeroes the window
and takes the deficit from the cells above, cell by cell, and fails if they cannot cover it
({{< code src/eos/fix_vapor_impl.h fix_vapor_impl >}}). @sec-ch10-fixvapor derives that branch.

This chapter does not port the repair. The search is a device kernel reached through a dispatch call, so a numpy port
would be a reimplementation. A check built on it would test the reimplementation and not the code. The conservation
properties above are read from the code and its comments. The ctests of @tbl-ch08-fixvapor-tests assert them on
fixed columns.

### Numerical method

The repair is the lambda at `split` ({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}). When the $x_1$ axis is split
across ranks it gathers the column first, but only on a call made with `whole_column` true. The two calls of the stage
pass it, after the multi-stage averaging and before the saturation adjustment (`whole_column`,
{{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}), and every block of the column then calls together.
The calls inside the equation-of-state conversions keep the default of `whole_column`, false
({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.hpp EquationOfStateImpl >}}), and repair only the block's own piece of the
column, so on a split axis their column-mass conservation holds per block piece.

The two callers are deliberately different, and the comment at `repair_column`
({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}) says why. Clouds tolerate a
column that cannot be repaired and fall back to a clamp at `clamp_min_`
({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}). Vapour must throw rather
than copy a bad gathered column back, which is the check at `err`
({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}). A failure in the vapour
path is therefore a hard stop, not a silent repair. On CUDA, inside a MeshBlock stage and in the conversion of
`check_redo`, the count is not read back at the call: the repair adds it to a 0-d device count, `vapor_failures_`,
which `check_redo` carries in its one device-to-host copy and raises there (@sec-ch07-redo); stage 0 zeroes it.
Every other call, and every call on the CPU, raises at once.

**The mark is on the deficit.** With marks enabled, the conserved pass copies the interior species rows before any
species repair (`species_before`, {{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}).
After the column repair it sets the patch mark of @sec-ch08-eoslimiter only where a species density was below
$-4096\,\epsilon_{\mathrm m}\lvert\rho\rvert$. Here $\rho$ is the cell's total gas density from those copied rows and
$4096\,\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$ is `species_repair_mark` of @sec-ch08-roundoff
({{< code src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp species_repair_mark >}}). How far the repair moved the donors does not enter
the test. A deficit below the bound is still repaired; it only does not ask for a redo.

**Why volumes, and why two callers.** Three facts of the code.

1. The redistribution weights by cell volume, so it moves mass and not density; moving densities would not conserve
   mass on a non-uniform grid
   ({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}).
2. When the $x_1$ axis is split across ranks the column is gathered first only for `whole_column` true, which the two
   stage calls pass. The conversions' calls repair the block's piece of the column, and conserve its mass there.
3. Clouds tolerate an unrepairable column and fall back to a clamp. Vapour must not copy a bad column back, so its
   caller passes `require_success` and the kernel's error becomes a hard stop.
4. The redo mark tests the deficit before the repair against $4096\,\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$ of the total gas density
   (`species_before`, {{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}), so a
   step is asked to be redone only when it left a species deficit above round-off, however the repair then spread it.

: Code map of the vapour column repair. {#tbl-ch08-fixvapor-code}

**How to use it.** There is no switch of its own. The vapour caller is this line, and the check after the
kernel is the failure a run sees
({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}):

```cpp
      TORCH_CHECK(!require_success || err == 0,
                  "[EquationOfState] apply_conserved_limiter_: "
                  "Failed to fix vapor mass fractions.");
```

```cpp
    repair_column(cons.index(interior).narrow(0, ICY, nvapor), true);
```

The borrow is these lines of `fix_vapor_impl` ({{< code src/eos/fix_vapor_impl.h fix_vapor_impl >}}), with `i` the
cell below the window and `is` its top:

```cpp
    T share = donors > 0. ? deficit / donors : T(0.);
    for (int j = is; j > i; --j) {
      vapor[j] = vapor[j] < 0. ? T(0.) : vapor[j] - vapor[j] * share;
    }
```

and the mark is these
({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}):

```cpp
      auto rho = cons.index(interior)[IDN] + species_before.sum(0);
      auto tol = species_repair_mark(cons.scalar_type()) * rho.abs();
      push_mark_(0, (species_before < -tol).any());
```

Refused: a vapour column that cannot be repaired, with the message above; a cloud column in the same state is
clamped at zero instead.

: Tests of the vapour column repair. {#tbl-ch08-fixvapor-tests}

The registrations are in {{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}}. No report check covers the repair.

`test_fix_vapor_deficit` puts vapour densities $2\times10^{-3}$, $1.5\times10^{-3}$, $10^{-3}$,
$-2.5\times10^{-11}$, $10^{-16}$, $10^{-16}$ kg m$^{-3}$ (bottom to top) over a dry density of $0.8$ kg m$^{-3}$
and runs the conserved pass once.[^ch08-fixvapor-run] The negative cell goes to $0$. The $10^{-3}$ cell, the only
donor of the window, goes to $9.9999997500000012\times10^{-4}$, a change of $-2.5\times10^{-11}$. The other four cells
are unchanged, the relative change of the column mass prints as $0$, and the step is marked. With the deficit set to
$1.82\times10^{-13}$, a quarter of the bound $7.28\times10^{-13}$, the donor moves by $-1.81899\times10^{-13}$ and the
step is not marked. The second command of the footnote ran `test_fix_vapor_volume`, `test_eos` and `test_forcing`
on the same build: every CPU case passed, in float32 and float64, and their CUDA cases were skipped. The three CPU
Python failure ctests, `test_fix_vapor_reports_failure_python`, `test_fix_vapor_counts_every_column_python` and
`test_fix_vapor_stale_count_python`, passed on the same build; their CUDA arms were not run.[^ch08-fixvapor-pyrun]

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- The vapour path throws when the column cannot be repaired (on CUDA within a stage, at `check_redo`). That is a crash, not a degraded run, and
  it is the intended behaviour rather than a defect.
- The repair sees the whole column only on the two stage calls, which pass `whole_column` true. On a split $x_1$
  axis those calls gather across ranks, so they are a collective operation inside what is otherwise a local limiter.
  The calls inside the equation-of-state conversions repair only the block's piece of a split column: a vapour
  deficit the piece cannot cover throws there even when the rest of the column could cover it.
:::

1. **Not ported.** The three properties of the Derivation are read from the code and asserted by ctests on fixed
   columns; no check in this chapter measures them on random columns.
2. **Proportional, not nearest-first.** Every donor of the window gives up the same fraction of its vapour, so a donor high in
   the window, next to the negative cell, gives no more than one far below it. Nothing in the repository measures
   whether a nearest-first borrow would change a run.
3. **Cost.** Gathering a column is communication inside the conserved pass of the two stage calls. Nothing in
   the repository measures how often it fires or what it costs.
